title: In-Situ ETEM Observations of Degradation in Cobalt Oxide Thermochemical Materials
content: Thermochemical materials (TCMs) are a promising class of materials for long duration energy storage (LDES) applications [1,2]. Conceptually similar to rechargeable electrochemical batteries, TCMs store and release energy as heat via reversible endo-/exo-thermic chemical reactions, acting as a thermal “battery”. High temperature TCMs specifically, with typical operating temperatures ranging from 300°C to above 1000°C, are being actively explored for capturing waste heat from industrial processes and for power generation [1–4]. However, degradation of TCMs upon repeated cycling at these elevated temperatures currently presents a major barrier that limits their viability for grid-scale implementation [4]. It is therefore critical to develop a fundamental understanding of degradation phenomena in high temperature TCMs that can then inform material design strategies to improve their reliability for long-term use in LDES systems.
